//replaceBlocks: PROOFREADING ROUND 1, comments #937 + #943 (one instruction, not two: the reviewer pasted the same 52-entry glossary twice — once on the contents page asking for it to be listed there, once on the last content page asking for the pages themselves). The manuscript ships no glossary at all, so this grafts one in as back matter. The anchor is the first block of the BACK COVER; it is replaced by the glossary followed by a verbatim `raw` copy of itself, which is how an append is expressed with replaceBlocks. `h1` gives the section its own page and a contents entry; the cts theme sets tocUnitsOnly:false, so the TOC line #937 asks for lands automatically after TOPIC 1.20 and needs no separate override. Entries are plain 'Term: meaning' paragraphs because formatGlossary() runs after applyOverrides() and styles them itself (bold term + ': ' + meaning), so the house glossary look is not hand-built here. //editAllExercise1: PROOFREADING ROUND 1, comment #939. The reviewer pasted an exercise to be inserted under LEARNING ACTIVITY 1, but the text they pasted is the storage-place exercise that is ALREADY EXERCISE 1 under LEARNING ACTIVITY 2 on the facing page — and they separately renumbered that existing box to EXERCISE 2 rather than deleting it, so applying the paste literally would have printed two near-identical storage exercises back to back, the first under a cleaning activity it has nothing to do with. Read instead as what actually differs between their version and the book's: the real answers. The manuscript's box only carries the rubric 'Learner correctly matches each item with its appropriate storage place', which tells a teacher nothing; the reviewer supplies the five matches. So the existing box is upgraded in place, under the activity it belongs to, and no exercise is added or renumbered. Decided with the user, who chose this reading over applying the paste verbatim. The reviewer's 'Expected Answer:'/'Expected Performance:' labels are deliberately NOT carried over - house style renders an expected answer as plain italic with no label, which the engine already does by stripping them.
//editAllActivityNumbers: QA PASS (not a reviewer comment). The book numbers its LEARNING ACTIVITY headings two different ways. In five of the eight topics that have more than one sub-topic (1.2, 1.8, 1.11, 1.13, 1.16) the activities run CONTINUOUSLY through the topic, so Topic 1.13 reads 1..6 straight across its two sub-topics. In two (1.3, 1.4) they restart at 1 in each sub-topic, so Topic 1.3 prints two separate 'LEARNING ACTIVITY 1' headings. Exercises, by contrast, run continuously in EVERY topic including these two - Topic 1.3's run 1..6 - so the restart is not a deliberate per-sub-topic scheme, just an inconsistency. House style is that the same element may not look different on different pages, so the two outliers are brought over to the majority's continuous numbering. Done as five surgical renames rather than with `renumberActivities`, for two reasons: that key resets its counter only at 'UNIT N' and 'LESSON N' banners, neither of which this primary family uses (it uses TOPIC/SUB-TOPIC), so it would number all 61 activities 1..61 across the whole book; and it would also silently renumber Topic 1.1, whose sequence is broken by a duplicated heading in the manuscript that is still with the reviewer - masking that defect instead of leaving it visible. Each `find` carries its activity's full title, and every one of those titles is unique in the book.
//editAllHeadingCase: QA PASS (not a reviewer comment). Four LEARNING ACTIVITY titles print out of step with the other 57, which are all Title Case. Two shout a single word mid-title (ACTIVITIES, ITEMS); the engine preserves an all-caps word inside an otherwise mixed heading in case it is an acronym, which is what correctly protects ICT elsewhere in this book, but neither of these is one. The manuscript is messier than that - six of its titles shout in full caps - but the engine's uniformBoxTitleCase pass already brings those over on the way out, so only these two survive into the PDF. `headingCase` was tried first and backed out: it is the documented key for settling a book's heading case, but on this book it fixed eight titles and broke nine, because TITLE_SMALL (which it uses) lists 'using' while the engine's own unasked pass explicitly refuses to lower it - 'never Using, a participle that title case capitalises' - so seven correct headings lost their capital, and its recase regex treats a hyphenated compound as a single word, flattening 'Role-Playing' to 'Role-playing' and 'Free-Form' to 'Free-form'. Two surgical renames are the smaller, safer change. NOTE the direction of the second one: this book capitalises Using everywhere else ('Making Products Using Hand Tools', 'Locating Landmarks Using Cardinal Points'), and this title only lost its capital because it arrived in full caps and was rebuilt through TITLE_SMALL - so it gains the capital back rather than its siblings losing theirs.
//topic11PlaygroundActivity: QA PASS (not a reviewer comment). TOPIC 1.1 printed two LEARNING ACTIVITY 3 headings, so its activities ran 1, 2, 3, 3, 4, 5. The second box is not a duplicate activity: it is the PLAYGROUND activity, pasted in under a second copy of the specialised-rooms heading together with that activity’s entire sixteen-line prologue. The importer shows it exactly — the second activity block opens with body items byte-identical to the first block’s complete body (Learner’s Book ref, materials, and all nine procedure steps), and only then begins its own material: playground equipment, its own eight-step procedure, its own Teacher’s Brief Notes, LET’S TALK AND LEARN, LET’S DO and EXERCISE 2. The manuscript settles what it is without anyone having to guess. Learner’s Book references run Page 4 for specialised rooms, pages 5–6 for this block (stated in its own Brief Notes), Pages 7–8 for the road and Pages 9–10 for posture — a continuous ascending sequence in which the playground is unambiguously the FOURTH activity of the topic, between specialised rooms and road safety. So the duplicated prologue is deleted, the block is renumbered 4, and the road and posture activities move to 5 and 6. INFERRED, and the one thing here not read off the manuscript: the wording of the new title. The block carries no title of its own, so it takes the parallel form of its sibling — “Practising Safety Rules in Specialised Rooms” becomes “Practising Safety Rules on the Playground”. If the author worded it differently in the syllabus, that line is the one to change. NOT fixed here, and still the reviewer’s: the topic’s EXERCISE numbering, which runs 1, 2, 3, 5. Every other topic in the book gives each activity exactly one exercise; this one now has six activities and four exercises, so exercises are genuinely missing rather than merely mis-numbered, and comments #940-942 cannot be applied until the author supplies them.

Name one ICT device you know.
Point to a computer or radio shown by your teacher.
Tell your teacher one use of a mobile phone.
With your teacher’s help, demonstrate how to switch an ICT device on or off, where appropriate.

blocks.para: *Answer: Press the correct power button with the teacher’s help.*

blocks.listitem: Should you handle ICT devices carefully? Say Yes or No.
Show how to take turns when using a shared device.

blocks.para: *Answer: Wait for your turn and allow others to use the device.*

blocks.listitem: Demonstrate how to put away or leave a device safely after use.

blocks.para: *Answer: Switch it off, where appropriate, and leave it in a safe place.*

blocks.listitem: What can you use to play an educational game on a computer?

blocks.para: a) Computer software  b) A school shoe  c) A cooking pot

blocks.listitem: Which device can run a computer game?

blocks.para: a) Computer  b) Broom  c) Chair

blocks.listitem: What should you do when the teacher gives instructions in the computer room?
Name one computer game or programme you have seen or used.
Point to the computer programme or game shown by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Point to the correct programme or game.*

blocks.listitem: Demonstrate how to sit properly when using a computer.

blocks.para: *Answer: Sit upright and face the computer screen.*

blocks.listitem: With your teacher’s help, take part in a simple educational computer game.

blocks.para: *Answer: Follow the instructions and play the game.*

blocks.listitem: Should you take turns when using a shared computer? Say Yes or No.
Show how you can treat a classmate fairly during a computer activity.

blocks.para: *Answer: Share the computer and take turns.*

blocks.listitem: Demonstrate how to follow the teacher’s instructions during a computer activity.

blocks.para: *Answer: Listen carefully and do what the teacher says.*

blocks.listitem: Which activity helps keep your body active?
Which activity involves jumping?

blocks.para: a) Frog jump  b) Reading  c) Drawing

blocks.listitem: What should you do before taking part in a physical activity?
Name one activity that helps keep your body fit.
Demonstrate deep breathing as shown by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Breathe in slowly and breathe out slowly.*

blocks.listitem: Perform a frog jump in a safe, open space.

blocks.para: *Answer: Bend your knees, place your hands on the floor and jump forward like a frog.*

blocks.listitem: Take part in a simple fitness activity guided by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Perform the activity by following the teacher’s instructions.*

blocks.listitem: Should you push other learners during exercise? Say Yes or No.
Show how to wait for your turn during a fitness activity.

blocks.para: *Answer: Stand in a line and wait quietly.*

blocks.listitem: Demonstrate how to follow the teacher’s safety instructions during exercise.

blocks.para: *Answer: Listen carefully and do what the teacher says.*

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a landmark?

blocks.para: a) A hospital  b) A pencil mark  c) A school exercise

blocks.listitem: Which activity can show a community’s culture?
Which direction is opposite to north?

blocks.para: a) East  b) South  c) West

blocks.listitem: Name one cultural activity in your community.
Name one landmark you know.
Show a traditional dance movement or sing a familiar cultural song, if you wish.

blocks.para: *Answer: Perform a simple traditional dance movement or sing a familiar cultural song.*

blocks.listitem: Using a simple map shown by your teacher, point to a landmark in the direction instructed.

blocks.para: *Answer: Point to the correct landmark on the map.*

blocks.listitem: Should you respect other people’s cultures? Say Yes or No.
Listen politely when a classmate talks about their culture.
Work with a group to share something you know about your community.

blocks.para: *Answer: Share information about a local landmark, traditional food, dance or song.*

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a game?

blocks.para: a) A running game  b) Sleeping  c) Eating lunch

blocks.listitem: Which activity is a track event?
What should you do when playing a game?
Name one game you know.
Demonstrate a simple running movement in a safe space.
Practise a simple jumping or throwing activity as directed by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Jump or throw carefully by following the teacher’s instructions.*

blocks.listitem: Take part in a simple game with your classmates.

blocks.para: *Answer: Play the game by following its rules.*

blocks.listitem: Should you accept the rules of a game? Say Yes or No.
Show how to take turns during a game.

blocks.para: *Answer: Wait for your turn and allow others to play.*

blocks.listitem: Demonstrate good sportsmanship when playing with others.

blocks.para: *Answer: Play fairly, share and respect others.*

blocks.listitem: Which tool is used to measure cloth?

blocks.para: a) Tape measure  b) Broom  c) Cup

blocks.listitem: Which tool can be used to mark cloth?

blocks.para: a) Tailor’s chalk  b) Plate  c) Ball

blocks.listitem: What should you do when using needlework tools?

blocks.para: b) Use them carefully with the teacher’s guidance
*Answer: b) Use them carefully with the teacher’s guidance.*

blocks.listitem: Name one small needlework tool.
Point to the tape measure shown by your teacher.
Draw a tailor’s chalk in your exercise book.

blocks.para: *Answer: Draw a simple picture of tailor’s chalk.*

blocks.listitem: Draw a thimble and show your drawing to the teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Draw a simple picture of a thimble.*

blocks.listitem: Should you play with needles or scissors? Say Yes or No.
Show how you would return needlework tools to their proper storage place.

blocks.para: *Answer: Put the tools in their correct storage place with the teacher’s help.*

blocks.listitem: Demonstrate how to share materials and follow the teacher’s instructions during a needlework activity.

blocks.para: *Answer: Share materials kindly, take turns and listen to the teacher.*
**Safety Note:** The teacher must supervise the activity. Sharp tools such as needles and scissors must be handled only with the teacher’s guidance.

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a type of line?

blocks.para: a) Zigzag  b) Spoon  c) Cup

blocks.listitem: Which tool can help you draw a straight line?

blocks.para: a) Ruler  b) Pillow  c) Plate

blocks.listitem: Why should we make lines clearly?

blocks.para: a) So people can see them easily
c) So nobody can see them
*Answer: a) So people can see them easily.*

blocks.listitem: Point to a straight line shown by your teacher.
Draw a straight line in your exercise book.

blocks.para: *Answer: Draw a neat straight line using a ruler.*

blocks.listitem: Draw a zigzag line.

blocks.para: *Answer: Draw a line with sharp turns.*

blocks.listitem: Draw a wavy line.

blocks.para: *Answer: Draw a line with smooth curves.*

blocks.listitem: Should you share drawing materials with others? Say Yes or No.
Show how to care for a ruler after using it.

blocks.para: *Answer: Wipe it clean and keep it safe.*

blocks.listitem: Arrange your drawing materials neatly after the activity.

blocks.para: *Answer: Put all drawing materials in their correct places.*

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a craft item?

blocks.para: a) A paper chain  b) A running race  c) A sound

blocks.listitem: Which material can be used to make a paper chain?

blocks.para: a) Paper  b) Water only  c) Sand only

blocks.listitem: What should you do with craft materials after using them?
Name one craft item you know.
Make a simple paper chain with your teacher’s guidance.

blocks.para: *Answer: Make paper loops and join them to form a chain.*

blocks.listitem: Use suitable materials to make a simple craft item.

blocks.para: *Answer: Make a simple item, such as a paper flower.*

blocks.listitem: Show your finished craft item to the class.
Should you respect another learner’s work? Say Yes or No.
Share craft materials with your group.

blocks.para: *Answer: Share materials kindly and take turns.*

blocks.listitem: Collect leftover materials and tidy your work area.

blocks.para: *Answer: Pick up leftover materials and put them in the correct places.*

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a letter?
Which item can you use to draw or write a letter?

blocks.para: a) Pencil  b) Plate  c) Shoe

blocks.listitem: What makes a letter easy to read?

blocks.para: a) Clear writing  b) Scribbling over it  c) Hiding it

blocks.listitem: Name one letter of the alphabet.
Write or copy the letter A in your exercise book.

blocks.para: *Answer: Write a neat capital letter A.*

blocks.listitem: Copy the letter B.

blocks.para: *Answer: Write a neat capital letter B.*

blocks.listitem: Colour a large letter provided by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Colour the letter neatly without going outside its outline.*

blocks.listitem: Should you take care of your pencils and crayons? Say Yes or No.
Share lettering materials with your classmates.

blocks.para: *Answer: Share materials kindly and take turns.*

blocks.listitem: Show how to keep your work neat and your materials tidy.

blocks.para: *Answer: Keep your work clean and put materials in their correct places.*

blocks.listitem: Where should you swim?

blocks.para: a) In a place approved for swimming with proper supervision
*Answer: a) In a place approved for swimming with proper supervision.*

blocks.listitem: What should you do before entering a swimming pool?

blocks.para: c) Push another learner into the water

blocks.listitem: Why should you shower before swimming, where required?

blocks.para: a) To help keep the pool clean
b) To make the floor dirty
c) To avoid listening to the teacher
*Answer: a) To help keep the pool clean.*

blocks.listitem: Name one item used for swimming.
Point to a swimming item shown by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Point to the correct swimming item.*

blocks.listitem: Show what you should do when the teacher says to wait before entering the pool.

blocks.para: *Answer: Stay out of the water and wait quietly.*

blocks.listitem: On dry land, demonstrate one action that shows you understand a swimming safety rule.

blocks.para: *Answer: Walk slowly and do not run near the pool.*

blocks.listitem: Should you enter water without permission and supervision? Say Yes or No.
Show how you can follow instructions during a swimming lesson.

blocks.para: *Answer: Listen carefully and do what the teacher says.*

blocks.listitem: Tell your teacher what you should do if you see another learner in danger near water.

blocks.para: *Answer: Tell the teacher or another adult immediately. Do not enter the water to rescue the learner.*

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a structure?

blocks.para: a) House  b) Song  c) Sound

blocks.listitem: What is a bridge used for?

blocks.para: a) Helping people cross an obstacle
*Answer: a) Helping people cross an obstacle.*

blocks.listitem: Which material can be used to make a simple model structure?

blocks.para: a) Building blocks  b) Sound  c) Light

blocks.listitem: Name one structure you see in your community.
Point to a picture of a house shown by your teacher.

blocks.para: *Answer: Point to the picture of the house.*

blocks.listitem: Draw a simple house in your exercise book.

blocks.para: *Answer: Draw a house with a roof, walls, a door and windows.*

blocks.listitem: Use safe materials or building blocks to make a simple model structure.

blocks.para: *Answer: Make a simple model house using building blocks or other safe materials.*

blocks.listitem: Should you destroy another learner’s model? Say Yes or No.
Work with your group to build a simple structure.

blocks.para: *Answer: Work together to build a simple model house.*

blocks.listitem: Put away the materials safely after completing your model.

blocks.para: *Answer: Return all materials to their correct places.*

blocks.para: c) A person who is swimming

blocks.listitem: Which of these is a good to sell?

blocks.para: a) A loaf of bread  b) A shadow  c) A sound

blocks.listitem: What should a seller do when a customer arrives?
Name one person who sells goods in your community.
Name one good that people buy.
Pretend to sell an item to a classmate.

blocks.para: *Answer: Say, “Welcome! I am selling a pencil.”*

blocks.listitem: Pretend to be a customer and ask politely for an item.

blocks.para: *Answer: Say, “Please, may I have a pencil?”*

Demonstrate how to take turns when playing a buying-and-selling game.

blocks.para: *Answer: Allow one learner to sell first, then change roles.*

blocks.listitem: Show how to treat a customer politely during the role-play.
